document_title: Since December 2023 a TEA scoring engine has read English STAAR written answers first, and reading rescore requests rose from 2,758 in spring 2024 to 64,489 this spring
_note: Caption carried verbatim from caption.txt. Slide strings polished from storyboard.md, each held to its claim quotes.
caption:
One written answer on a STAAR reading test.

Since December 2023 a Texas Education Agency scoring engine has read the written answers on English STAAR tests first. Its design then sent at least 25 percent to people too. Their score counted. TEA says hand scoring would cost $15 million to $20 million more a year.

Then districts asked for a person. Reading rescore requests rose from 2,758 in spring 2024 to 64,489 this spring, the Texas Tribune reported October 7th. People did every rescore. More than 13,300 scores went up. In Dallas ISD 34% of more than 5,100 tests came back higher.

Fewer than half of one percent of all open-ended reading answers changed.

A rescore costs a district $50 a test unless the score changes.

TEA's design dates to December 2023 and March 2024. Does it still describe this spring's scoring?

#STAAR #TexasEducationAgency #DallasISD

S1.headline: A machine reads English STAAR answers first
S1.body: Since December 2023 an automated scoring engine has scored the written answers on English STAAR tests first, the Texas Education Agency says. The machine is drawn to illustrate.
strings: A machine reads English STAAR answers first
Since December 2023 an automated scoring engine has scored the written answers on English STAAR tests first, the Texas Education Agency says. The machine is drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: Six to seven times the written answers
S2.body: TEA says STAAR now brings 6 to 7 times more written answers a year. Scoring them all by hand would cost $15 million to $20 million more a year and take four to five times as many scorers.
strings: Six to seven times the written answers
TEA says STAAR now brings 6 to 7 times more written answers a year. Scoring them all by hand would cost $15 million to $20 million more a year and take four to five times as many scorers.

S3.headline: People scored what it was built on
S3.body: TEA says each question's engine is programmed on about 3,000 field test answers scored by people. The agency calls it a closed database whose student answers only TEA can access. The drawer is drawn to illustrate.
strings: People scored what it was built on

TEA says each question's engine is programmed on about 3,000 field test answers scored by people. The agency calls it a closed database whose student answers only TEA can access. The drawer is drawn to illustrate.

S4.headline: At least one in four also goes to a person
S4.body: As TEA described it in December 2023 and March 2024, every written answer goes through the engine and at least 25 percent are also scored by people. Where a person scores an answer, that score counts. Drawn to illustrate.
strings: At least one in four also goes to a person

As TEA described it in December 2023 and March 2024, every written answer goes through the engine and at least 25 percent are also scored by people. Where a person scores an answer, that score counts. Drawn to illustrate.

S5.headline: Then the requests multiplied
S5.body: Requests to regrade reading answers went from 2,758 in spring 2024 to 21,620 a year later and 64,489 this spring, the Texas Tribune reported. That is more than 23 times the 2024 count. One sheet stands for one request, drawn to illustrate.
strings: Requests to regrade reading answers went from 2,758 in spring 2024 to 21,620 a year later and 64,489 this spring, the Texas Tribune reported. That is more than 23 times the 2024 count. One sheet stands for one request, drawn to illustrate.

S6.headline: People did every rescore
S6.body: TEA sends rescore requests to human scorers, and the Tribune reports people did all of them. Written answers on Spanish STAAR tests are scored by people alone. Drawn to illustrate.
strings: TEA sends rescore requests to human scorers, and the Tribune reports people did all of them. Written answers on Spanish STAAR tests are scored by people alone. Drawn to illustrate.

S7.headline: More than 13,300 reading scores went up
S7.body: The state raised them after the reviews, the Tribune reported. Across every open-ended reading answer, fewer than half of one percent changed. The single gilded page in 200 is drawn to illustrate.
strings: More than 13,300 reading scores went up

S8.headline: In Dallas ISD 34% came back higher
S8.body: The district sent more than 5,100 reading tests for rescoring, the Tribune reported. Each tile on this Dallas County relief is one in a hundred, drawn to illustrate.

S9.headline: A district can ask for a person
S9.body: A rescore costs $50 a test if the score holds, and TEA waives the fee when it changes. TEA's scoring documents and the Texas Tribune's October 7th report have the detail.
